narrative_purpose: The figure makes learned ecological memory spatial: an elder killer whale leads descendants along a route that exists in her experience rather than on the surface of the sea.
subject: An older female killer whale with a slightly worn dorsal fin leads a multi-generational pod of six anatomically correct killer whales through sparse dark water. Two juveniles and three adults follow her curved path. Far ahead, a narrow distant school of salmon catches faint cyan light near an underwater shelf; the rest of the sea appears nearly empty. A subtle trail of fading bioluminescent particles marks only the route already taken, not a drawn arrow.
scene: Cold open ocean during a lean season, deep indigo water with a dim rocky shelf and very little prey outside the one distant school.
camera: High oblique naturalist view looking down and forward along the pod's curved formation, elder prominent at lower left and prey distant at upper right.
light: Low cool ambient light, cyan rim on black-and-white bodies, faint teal route particles and a sparse amber focus on the distant salmon school.
palette: Void indigo water, stone white and charcoal animals, cyan-teal edges, very small amber prey accent.
style: Painterly behavioral-ecology plate, quiet and spatially legible rather than dramatic wildlife spectacle.
detail_level: Crisp elder, followers and distant prey; water and seabed simplified into layered haze with label-ready negative space.
composition: A diagonal route from elder to prey, followers visibly ordered behind her, empty water emphasizing that the valuable feature is knowledge rather than abundance.
consistency_notes: Use anatomically accurate Earth killer whales. The elder is identifiable by position and gently worn fin, not exaggerated age or human facial expression.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no map overlay, no anthropomorphic expressions, no photographic or CGI look, no giant prey swarm, no cartoon style
